subject: Regional anchoring & acceptable transient egress windows for analytics workload
messages:
From: Sarah Patel <sarah@medicapps.com>

Subject: Regional anchoring requirements for PHI analytics pipeline

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking this — MedicApps is evaluating Redwood to power our analytics pipeline that will process PHI-derived telemetry. Before we move further we need written commitments around where data will be stored and processed. High level asks: 

- Data residency: customer data must be kept in EU for storage and primary processing.
- Transient processing: occasional analytics bursts (up to 4x/month, each up to a few hours) may touch non-EU compute for cost reasons. We need to understand if Redwood supports an explicit temporary egress window and how that would be documented/limited.
- Subprocessors: complete roster and notification policy.
- KMS / key control: can we require our own key for tenant encryption?
- Evidence: SOC2 or audit artifacts, and a short security questionnaire (attached).

Attached: medicapps-security-questionnaire.pdf

Can you confirm Redwood's options (hosted/dedicated/private) and what contractual addenda you propose for the above? Also please point us to the subprocessor roster and any limits on transient cross-border processing.

Thanks,
Sarah Patel
Head of Platform Security
MedicApps

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah@medicapps.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Regional anchoring requirements for PHI analytics pipeline

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list and the questionnaire. Looping in Kimberly (legal/DPAs) and Rishi (infrastructure) so we can give an authoritative answer.

Short answers up front:
- Yes, we can support EU-anchored storage and primary processing.
- We offer three deployment patterns that map to different guarantees: Hosted (fastest onboarding), Dedicated (reserved EU-only GPU pools), and Private (VPC/on-prem for strict sovereignty).
- For hosted customers requiring EU-first residency we provide a configurable "regional anchoring" mode with documented allowable transient egress windows.
- Tenant KMS (BYOK) is available on Dedicated and Private; hosted can support customer-managed envelope keys in many cases.

Next steps: can you share approximate QPS, peak tokens/hour for the bursts, and whether those bursts are asynchronous batch analytics vs real-time inference? That will help us size Dedicated pools or propose transient egress SLAs.

We reviewed the questionnaire and started filling it out — we'll return a redlined DPA addendum and the subprocessors roster. In the meantime, see the short notes below on transient egress logic and safeguards: 

- Regional anchoring vs strict binding: "anchoring" means data-at-rest and primary requests are kept in-region; we allow pre-authorized failover/analytics windows to compatible regions under monitored conditions. "Strict binding" (no cross-border processing) is available via Private deployment.
- Transient egress windows: typical packaged option is up to 6 hours/month for maintenance/analytics with audit logs and customer notification; we can negotiate the window and frequency in the addendum.
- Controls during egress window: per-tenant encryption keys (BYOK), KMS audit logs, per-request metadata capturing processing-region, and automatic rollback/reprocessing guidance if required.
- Subprocessors: AWS EU regions, GCP europe-west, and our CDN/monitoring partners (full roster to follow).

We'll attach the partial questionnaire answers and the current subprocessor CSV in the next message.

Best,
Grace
Director, Compliance & Risk
Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah / Tom,

Appreciate the scope. Based on the burst profile (asynchronous batch, ~5M tokens/hour, 2-3x/month) we recommend the following pragmatic path that balances cost and contractual certainty: 

1) Immediate onboarding (Hosted, EU-anchored):
   - We enable "regional anchoring" for your tenant: primary storage and request routing remain in EU (europe-west).
   - A documented transient egress allowance: up to 8 hours/month by default for analytics and maintenance, can be reduced to 4 hours/month in the DPA addendum. Emergency increases possible with 24-hour notice; for true emergency (ops/security) we allow ad-hoc escalation with post-facto customer notification and justification.

2) Optional near-term upgrade (Dedicated EU pool):
   - If you want cryptographic separation and stronger SLA, Dedicated provides reserved EU-only GPU capacity and supports HSM-backed BYOK with customer keys never exportable from your tenancy.

3) Private deployment:
   - For strict non-crossborder processing guarantees (no transient egress allowed), Private deployment or on-prem is the recommended contractual solution.

Security and operational controls we will include in the addendum: 
- Per-request region metadata in audit logs; full audit log retention for 12 months (longer on request).
- BYOK/HSM support on Dedicated/Private; hosted with envelope keys and strict access controls.
- Subprocessor notification: 30-day notice for new subprocessors that affect EU processing; immediate notification for critical security incidents.
- Evidence: SOC2 Type II report available under NDA; we will also provide the redlined DPA addendum via DocuSign.

Attachments and next steps:
- Attached: redwood-subprocessor-roster-2026-07.csv (current roster), redwood-dpa-addendum-docuSign-link.txt (DocuSign link to sign).
- I'll have Kimberly prepare a short SOW clause for the transient egress windows (definitions and metrics) and Rishi will provide a short ops playbook for how we route bursts and capture metadata.

If those items look acceptable I'll circulate the DocuSign link and a proposed amendment that captures the 4-hour vs 8-hour options and BYOK details.
